Incorporating the July 2020 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, the FOMC’s highly accommodative stance (ZLB, ongoing Treasury/agency MBS purchases, and new average inflation targeting) is counterbalanced by clear evidence of tighter bank credit and softer loan demand:

- Banks reported widespread tightening of standards and terms for C&I loans to firms of all sizes, with many expecting further tightening over the remainder of 2020.
- CRE lending standards tightened notably, with weaker demand.
- Consumer credit (credit card, auto, and other) saw substantial tightening and weaker demand; residential mortgage demand was strong but underwriting tightened.
- These tighter bank lending conditions imply that, despite supportive monetary policy, the flow of credit to more vulnerable borrowers could be constrained, weighing on the recovery.

Net: Relative to an FSR-only read, SLOOS tilts the balance further negative. The tone remains accommodative but risk-aware, with credit supply frictions and weaker demand reinforcing downside risks.
